newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile shares end soft, seen rising on rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Chile shares end soft, seen rising on rate cut.

text.p: Chilean stocks skidded to close over one percent lower, tracking Wall Street, but the bolsa is expected to rally gently Monday on news of the Central Bank's long-awaited interest rate cut, said dealers.
"There will be some rebound, but it is unlikely to be significant," said Henry Rudnick, head of research at brokerage CB Capitales.
"The market had already assumed that rates were going to come down."
The index ended down 1.09 percent at 118.32 points.
The general index shed 0.63 percent to 5,376.99 points in turnover of 13.6 billion pesos.
News of the bank's 0.25 percentage point cut in interest rates came after the market closed, although it had been widely rumoured for weeks.
Traders said there could be some profit taking Monday with players cashing in gains from sharp rises in recent sessions.

Steel-maker Cap is expected to rally next week following remarks from president Roberto de Andraca that the company expected to report first quarter earnings 50-80 percent higher than in the same period last year.
"No-one was expecting profits to rise so steeply. It was a surprise," said Rudnick.
Cap ended down 2.6 percent at 1,125 pesos.
Other losers included telecom Telex, down 3.96 percent at 1,090 pesos and brewery CCU, which shed 2.25 percent to 1,740 pesos.
Winners included airline LanChile, up seven percent at 610 pesos and publisher Cochrane, which gained 3.57 percent to 145 pesos.
